cards.title: Standard Error Calculation for Sparse AUC and Cmax
cards.claim: Standard errors for mean Cmax and AUC are calculated to account for correlations from repeated sampling of individual animals. SE for Cmax is the sample standard deviation of y-values at Tmax divided by sqrt(n). SE for AUC uses a method (Nedelman and Jia 1998; Holder 2001) involving sample variances and covariances between time points.
conditions: Sparse sampling with repeated measures on subjects
Linear trapezoidal rule used for AUC
required_inputs: Subject IDs to identify repeated measures
limitations: Requires calculation of sample covariance between concentrations at different times.
If r_ij=1 and r_i=1 or r_j=1, covariance s_ij is set to 0.
cards.downstream_use: Interpreting uncertainty in sparse PK parameters; understanding how software handles correlated errors.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
